top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu alone) is the only proposal that names a laureate, and on the common literary criteria it is the best-supported case in the record. His voice is distinctive. As publicly described, Blinding and Solenoid build very large prose structures in which memory, the body and dream form one continuing metaphysical project, and the work spans decades and several large books, so it does not rest on a single title. The main reservation is unresolved: whether Solenoid reorganizes the earlier Orbitor architecture or restates it. I hold my reading that it changes the mode as provisional and unverified by close reading. The judgment of Romanian prose rests on translation and public knowledge, and the coverage of his poetry is thin. The citation should therefore be scoped to the novels, with poetry only as lyric ground, and should credit architecture and imaginative invention more than sentence-level music. I do not rely on the shared round-1 first places as evidence of merit, since they may reflect correlated reasoning from the same public knowledge. I do not rely on the 'idealist' direction of Nobel's will either. I rank P000 (no award) last because the case, though provisional, is strong enough, and no stated condition, such as close reading or expert reports showing the later fictions only restate the earlier ones, has been shown to hold.
